I’ll use the current tracker prototype inputs. The comparison will include the original ODD layout and the extended layout before and after the recorded DES018 pixel ring removal. The IdRes model will use pitch/√12 resolution and the existing prototype’s per-layer material allowances; those material curves are a parametric comparison, not a full DD4hep material scan.

The JSON reductions are ready: 48 ideal layers for original ODD and 52 for each extended case. One reporting detail matters here: IdRes classifies the prototype’s 0.5 mm short-strip segmentation as “pixel-like.” I’ll therefore save technology counts from the JSON metadata alongside IdRes’s raw counts, so the plots identify pixel, short-strip, and long-strip hits correctly.

All 64,881 IdRes fit rows completed, and the 54 near-zero-material controls agree with the independent covariance calculation at IdRes’s printed precision.

The aperture variant preserves the extended layout’s hits and resolution across the sampled |η| ≤ 4 grid. The extension improves forward curvature information, but at 100 GeV the η ≈ 4 uncertainty is still too large to interpret as a Gaussian fractional momentum resolution. I’m making that limit explicit in the plots and documentation.

The seven SVGs and complete CSV/JSON tables are now saved, including raw IdRes inputs and outputs, source hashes, and regeneration commands. I’m finishing the artifact and repository checks, then I’ll push the documentation branch and open the PR.

The local checks pass, including regeneration of the geometry JSON and all seven SVGs from the saved inputs. The documentation explains the hit-count conventions, material assumptions, and momentum-resolution limits. I’m publishing the PR now.
